title: SQL injection via string concatenation
description: User-controlled request parameter flows into a SQL query built via string concatenation, allowing an attacker to alter query semantics.
impact: An attacker can read, modify, or delete arbitrary rows in the users table, and potentially escalate to full database compromise.
technical_analysis: The handler concatenates req.params.id directly into the WHERE clause of a raw SQL string instead of using a parameterized query or query builder placeholder.
poc_description: Sending id=1 OR 1=1 as the request parameter returns all rows instead of a single user.
remediation_steps: Validate that the id parameter is numeric before use
evidence: query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=' + req.params.id  // debug token sk-abcDEF0123456789ghijklmnop
assumptions: Assumes the users table is reachable from the request handler without additional authorization checks.

code_locations.snippet:
const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=' + req.params.id;
const row = db.get(query);
code_locations.label: vulnerable query construction
code_locations.fix_before: const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=' + req.params.id;
code_locations.fix_after: const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=?'; const row = db.get(query, [req.params.id]);

title: Reflected XSS in search results page
description: The search term from the query string is rendered into the results page without HTML-escaping, allowing script injection.
impact: An attacker can craft a link that executes arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser session (session theft, phishing, defacement).
technical_analysis: res.send() interpolates the raw `q` query parameter into an HTML template string without escaping special characters.
poc_description: Navigating to /search?q=<script>alert(1)</script> executes the injected script.
remediation_steps: Escape user input before interpolating into HTML, or use a templating engine with auto-escaping enabled.
